notes.meaning: The Messiah announces that God's Spirit rests upon Him for a special mission. God has anointed Him—which means setting Him apart—to bring the good news of rescue to those who are poor, crushed in spirit, and trapped by sin. Jesus read these words aloud in Nazareth to show that His saving work had begun.

other.label: Modern scholarship
other.view: Many modern scholars understand the speaker to be the prophet Isaiah describing his own calling to comfort the exiles, rather than the Messiah speaking directly.

notes.meaning: The speaker announces a time of God’s favor, like a year of jubilee when debts are cancelled and captives are freed. He also proclaims that God will judge the powers of evil and comfort all who are grieving over sin. Jesus stopped reading this passage before the day of vengeance, showing that this time of grace comes first.

God promises to trade the sorrow of His people for joy. Instead of ashes on their heads from mourning, they receive a beautiful crown, fragrant oil of gladness, and robes of praise. God strengthens them to become like great oak trees of righteousness, living in a way that honors Him.

The people set free by God will rebuild ruined cities and repair homes that have been abandoned for generations. This applied first to the Jewish exiles returning from Babylon to rebuild their homeland. It also shows how God works through His people to restore lives that have been damaged by sin.

Foreigners and outsiders will come alongside God's people to tend their sheep and work their fields. God's people had once been treated as slaves, but now others gladly help with their daily labor. This allows God's people to keep their hearts focused on serving the Lord instead of being trapped by worldly worries.

Instead of being worn down by field chores, God's people are given the high honor of serving as His priests and ministers. Surrounding nations will bring their wealth and gifts to support the worship of God. In the church, all believers are invited to share in this calling as a royal priesthood.

God promises His people double honor and blessing in place of the shame and disgrace they suffered. In Bible times, the oldest son received a double portion of the family inheritance, showing special favor. God gives His restored people an enduring inheritance filled with everlasting joy.

The Lord explains that He will rescue His people because He loves justice and hates all wicked robbery. Because God is completely faithful, He will reward their suffering and make an everlasting covenant—an unbreakable promise—with them. Real worship must include treating people fairly, because rituals never excuse doing wrong.

The children and descendants of God's people will be widely known and respected among all nations. Everyone who sees them will clearly recognize that God has blessed them with His goodness and favor. Godly families show the world what God's grace looks like in everyday life.

The speaker bursts into joyful praise because God has clothed His people with salvation and wrapped them in a robe of righteousness, which means being made right with God. This spiritual clothing is compared to a bridegroom wearing a priestly crown or a bride putting on her finest jewels. Believers can rejoice because this righteousness is a gift from God rather than something earned by good works.

Just as seeds in the soil naturally sprout and grow into a lush garden, the Lord will cause righteousness and praise to grow across all nations. God Himself gives the power for this spiritual life to flourish and spread. His salvation will not remain hidden, but will bear visible fruit throughout the world.
